elements.quote: The declaration of nutrition information on the label and in labeling of a food shall contain information about the level of the following nutrients, except for those nutrients whose inclusion
elements.note: Paragraph (c)(1)-(c)(8) enumerates the nutrients in order and marks voluntary ones as (VOLUNTARY); the mandatory list is the unmarked entries (calories, total fat, saturated fat, trans fat, cholesterol, sodium, total carbohydrate, dietary fiber, total sugars, added sugars, protein, and the vitamins/minerals in (c)(8)(ii)), several with low-level exemptions.

elements.quote: A statement of the number of grams of added sugars in a serving, except that label declaration of added sugars content is not required for products that contain less than 1 gram of added sugars
elements.note: Mandatory, subject to the <1 g / no-claim exemption; rounding to nearest gram also stated in (c)(6)(iii).

elements.quote: The declaration of vitamins and minerals as a quantitative amount by weight and percent of the RDI shall include vitamin D, calcium, iron, and potassium in that order
elements.note: Text also includes calcium and iron, which J does not name; (c)(8)(iii) allows omission below 2 percent of the RDI with a 'Not a significant source' statement.

elements.element: increment and rounding rules per nutrient
elements.quote: expressed to the nearest 5-calorie increment up to and including 50 calories, and 10-calorie increment above 50 calories, except that amounts less than 5 calories may be expressed as zero
elements.note: Each nutrient subparagraph in (c) states its own increment, e.g. sodium (c)(4): 'to the nearest 5-milligram increment when the serving contains 5 to 140 milligrams of sodium'; vitamins/minerals percent (c)(8)(iii): 'The percentages for vitamins and minerals shall be expressed to the nearest 2-percent increment up to and including the 10-percent level'. The (c)(8)(iv) RDI/units table content is not present in the evidence text (only its lead-in sentence).

completeness_note: All J elements are stated within 101.9(c). Rounding of percent Daily Value for macronutrients appears in 101.9(d)(7)(ii) (visible in the truncated whole-section text: 'with the percent expressed to the nearest whole percent for each nutrient declared'), which G does not cite; J does not expressly ask for %DV rounding, so not flagged as an omission.
rationale: 101.9(c) lists the mandatory and voluntary nutrients in order, including added sugars, vitamin D and potassium, and states the rounding increment for each nutrient; every J element is found in the cited paragraph.
uncertainty: J is terse ('Mandatory nutrient list'); an SME may expect the answer to include %DV rounding in 101.9(d)(7)(ii) or the (c)(8)(iv) RDI units table, which is not reproduced in the evidence text.
needs_research_items: Optional: SME to decide whether 101.9(d)(7)(ii) (%DV rounding) should be added to G for a complete rounding answer.

elements.element: Dual-column labeling per serving and per container
elements.quote: must provide an additional column within the Nutrition Facts label that lists the quantitative amounts and percent Daily Values for the entire package
elements.note: Applies to products 'packaged and sold individually' containing at least 200 percent and up to and including 300 percent of the reference amount; second column is per serving derived from the reference amount. For discrete units, (b)(2)(i)(D) requires a parallel per-serving and per-unit dual column.

elements.quote: The first column would be based on the serving size for the product and the second column would be based on the entire contents of the package.
elements.note: Column order requirement; (b)(12)(ii) adds a claim-basis statement requirement when claims appear on dual-column labels.

elements.quote: This provision does not apply to raw fruits, vegetables, and seafood for which voluntary nutrition labeling is provided in the product labeling or advertising or when claims are made about the product
elements.note: (A) excludes products eligible for the (j)(13)(ii)(A)(1)/(2) small-package formats; (C) excludes products already bearing certain additional columns and varied-weight products.

completeness_note: The governing text is 101.9(b)(12)(i) (and (b)(2)(i)(D) for discrete units), both within the cited 101.9(b). 101.12 supplies the reference amounts (RACC) against which the 200-300 percent range is measured; its evidence text contains no dual-column rule but is a reasonable supporting cite.
rationale: 101.9(b)(12)(i) requires dual-column (per serving and per entire package) labeling for individually packaged products at 200-300 percent of the RACC and lists exemptions in (A)-(C); this is inside the cited 101.9(b).
uncertainty: G cites 101.9(b) broadly rather than the pinpoint (b)(12)(i); an SME may prefer the pinpoint. The question says 'container' while the rule is framed as products 'packaged and sold individually'; discrete-unit products fall under (b)(2)(i)(D) (per-unit column) instead.
needs_research_items: Optional: SME to decide whether to tighten G to '21 CFR 101.9(b)(12)(i) and (b)(2)(i)(D); 101.12(b)'.
